SOURCE.quote: The software should not drop checks that need no key, including tail-truncation detection, when a halt occurs.
SOURCE.covered: Not that clause, but the contract this function keeps while reading the log for it: a line that cannot be read does not leave the function as a successful list of the lines before it.
notCovered: The clause itself: which checks keep running past a halt, and whether tail truncation is among them. That is the loop in `verify`, not this one.
What `show_entries` prints for the entries it did read.
Every other path that reads the same log.

on_error_control.instructions: `code` is one function that walks an iterator whose items are each either a value or an error. Take the case where one item is an error. What does the function do with the items after it?

criteria.stops_there: It stops at that item; the ones after it are never taken from the iterator
criteria.keeps_going: It goes on taking the items after it
criteria.cannot_determine: The code does not say what happens to the items after an error

on_error_result.instructions: Still `code`, still the case where one item is an error. What does the function return to its caller?

criteria.an_error: A failure — whatever the caller does with it, it is not a successful list
criteria.a_success_with_what_it_had: A success carrying the items it managed to take, without the failure
criteria.cannot_determine: The code does not say what is returned when an item is an error

an_error.why: the failed enumeration does not leave the function as a success

a_success_with_what_it_had.why: the entries taken before the error are returned as though the listing were complete

a_success_with_nothing.why: an enumeration that failed is returned as an empty listing

cannot_determine.why: the code shown does not say what is returned
